purpose: Phenytoin is used to prevent and control seizures. It is commonly prescribed for people with epilepsy or for those who have had seizures after brain surgery or a head injury. It helps keep seizures from happening or makes them less severe.
how_it_works: Your brain works by sending electrical signals between nerve cells. When those signals go haywire, a seizure can happen. Phenytoin works by calming down those overactive electrical signals in the brain, helping to keep them steady and controlled so seizures are less likely to occur.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include dizziness, drowsiness, and feeling unsteady or clumsy. You might also notice slurred speech, nausea, or constipation. With long-term use, some people develop swollen or overgrown gums, increased hair growth on the body, or coarsening of facial features. It can also cause your urine to turn pink or reddish-brown, which is harmless.
warnings: Do not stop taking phenytoin suddenly — this can trigger serious seizures. Phenytoin can cause a rare but severe skin reaction, so call your doctor right away if you develop a rash. It can also affect your liver, so regular blood tests are important. This medication can interact with many other drugs and can be harmful during pregnancy. Avoid alcohol while taking it, as it can affect how the drug works in your body.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is between 300 mg and 400 mg per day, often taken in divided doses. Your doctor will start you on a lower dose and slowly adjust it based on your blood levels and how you respond. It is very important to take it at the same time every day and never miss a dose. Your doctor will check blood levels regularly to make sure you are getting the right amount.
